source: Historical Atlas by William R. Shepherd (Henry Holt, 1911) — public domain, scanned by the University of Texas Libraries.

plates.title: Reference Map of Ancient Palestine
plates.note: The land itself at the greatest detail in the atlas — towns, districts, roads and relief, with insets of Jerusalem and the allotments of the tribes.

plates.title: Mycenean Greece and the Orient about 1450 B.C.
plates.when: c. 1450 BC — the patriarchs and the Exodus
plates.note: Egypt, Canaan and the Hittites as they stood before the conquest, with the Nile delta drawn out.

plates.title: The Assyrian Empire and the Region about the Eastern Mediterranean, 750–625 B.C.
plates.when: 750–625 BC — the divided kingdom and the fall of Samaria
plates.note: The empire that took the northern kingdom away, with the provinces it broke Israel into.

plates.title: The Oriental Empires about 600 B.C.
plates.when: c. 600 BC — Babylon, and the exile
plates.note: Babylon at its height, the road the exiles walked, and Judah as a fragment on its western edge.

plates.title: Greek and Phoenician Settlements in the Mediterranean Basin, about 550 B.C.
plates.note: Where Tyre and Sidon actually reached, which is how far Tarshish and the ships of the prophets went.

plates.title: The Macedonian Empire, 336–323 B.C.
plates.when: 336–323 BC — Alexander, and the kingdoms after him
plates.note: Alexander's march and the four kingdoms his generals cut it into — the world between the Testaments.

plates.title: Reference Map of Asia Minor under the Greeks and Romans
plates.when: the Roman province system, 1st century AD
plates.note: Every province and city Paul crossed, at the detail the journeys need — Galatia, Pontus, Bithynia and the seven churches.

plates.title: Plan of Imperial Rome, with the Plan of Athens
plates.note: The two cities the New Testament ends in, street by street — the Areopagus, and the Rome Paul was brought to.

plates.title: Development of Christianity to 1300
plates.note: Where the church actually spread, century by century, and how far east it went before it went north.

plates.title: The Roman and Hunnic Empires about 450
plates.note: The empire the early councils met inside, at the moment it began to come apart.
